clue.text: Understand new paper that leads to hospital closure

indicators.note: new signals that the letters of paper are made over into a fresh order

parts.note: H is the standard abbreviation for hospital, as on road signs
a closure is an end or finish

explanation.surface: Someone grasps that a fresh newspaper story will lead to a hospital being shut down.
explanation.walkthrough: 'new' is the anagram signal; 'closure' looks like the hospital shutting, but just means an end, tacked on after H.
explanation.definitionFit: To grasp a meaning is to understand it, the mental sense of seize.

clue.text: Beans, say, taken by sister?

explanation.surface: A nurse helping herself to a plate of beans.
explanation.walkthrough: In Britain a senior nurse is called Sister, and nurses take a patient's heartbeat reading.
explanation.definitionFit: Beans and lentils are edible seeds known collectively by this name; a heartbeat felt at the wrist is what a nurse takes.

clue.text: Right behind 15 beam

parts.note: behind, in the sense of later or following, means after

explanation.surface: Someone stands just behind a structural beam.
explanation.walkthrough: The '15' is a cross-reference in the printed grid to another light; it plays no part in the wordplay here.
explanation.definitionFit: A sloping roof timber is one kind of beam.

clue.text: Henry quarrel in school?

parts.note: H is the symbol for the henry, the unit of inductance
a quarrel is a bolt shot from a crossbow, a kind of arrow

explanation.surface: A boy named Henry gets into a row at school.
explanation.walkthrough: 'quarrel' looks like an argument but means a crossbow bolt. HARROW is a famous English public school in north-west London.
explanation.definitionFit: Harrow School is an example of an English boarding school, hence the question mark.

clue.text: Mark in the nick

explanation.surface: A man called Mark sits in a prison cell.
explanation.walkthrough: 'nick' is British slang for prison, but here it means a small cut.
explanation.definitionFit: A small V-shaped cut is both a mark and a nick.

clue.text: Hang back purposely in enlarged shoes, repaired

indicators.note: repaired suggests the letters are taken apart and put back together differently

explanation.surface: Someone dawdles deliberately in shoes that were stretched when mended.
explanation.walkthrough: 'repaired' shuffles the thirteen letters of ENLARGED SHOES.
explanation.definitionFit: To delay deliberately is the idiomatic sense of this phrase, picturing feet dragged reluctantly.

clue.text: Gourmet with an alternative that is most appetizing

indicators.note: alternative suggests a different arrangement of the letters before it

explanation.surface: A food lover is offered another option that looks the most delicious.
explanation.walkthrough: 'alternative' rearranges GOURMET WITH AN, thirteen letters in all.
explanation.definitionFit: Food so tempting it makes saliva flow is extremely appetizing.

clue.text: Build-up of people in favour of time-share?

parts.note: a pro is someone in favour of something, as in pros and cons
a lifetime, one's span of time, is a life
a ration is an allotted share

explanation.surface: Supporters of timeshare holiday homes are multiplying.
explanation.walkthrough: 'time-share' looks like a holiday property but splits into two separate synonyms; 'people in favour' are the pros of pros and cons.
explanation.definitionFit: A rapid increase in numbers is a build-up.

clue.text: Old weapons put out over ships' stems

indicators.note: in a down clue, over places the first piece on top of the next

parts.note: to be put out is to be annoyed or cross
the stem of a ship is its bow

explanation.surface: Ancient arms are unloaded above the prows of vessels.
explanation.definitionFit: Medieval archers used these mechanical bows as weapons.

clue.text: Do they provide river digs of the lighter kind?

definitions.text: Do they provide river digs of the lighter kind?

parts.words: Do they provide river digs of the lighter kind?
parts.note: digs is British slang for lodgings, and an apartment is a flat; lighter is both a barge and a word for less heavy, so this asks about level-bottomed river craft

explanation.surface: A question about floating lodgings on a river.
explanation.definitionFit: Shallow-draught river vessels are lighters, playing on flat as a home.

clue.text: Blackguard has to go back in regret

indicators.note: in places one piece within the other

parts.note: to rue something is to regret it

indicators.note: back signals that the word go is read backwards

parts.note: go is used as written

explanation.surface: A scoundrel has to leave and goes back full of remorse.
explanation.walkthrough: 'back' turns GO into OG, which goes 'in' RUE.
explanation.definitionFit: A blackguard is a scoundrel or rascal.

clue.text: Torrid at the Spanish watering-hole

parts.note: torrid means very hot
el is the Spanish for the

explanation.surface: Sweltering heat at the Spanish oasis.
explanation.definitionFit: A watering-hole is jocular slang for a place to drink, such as a bar or inn.

clue.text: Low sound to develop at length

parts.note: to develop is to grow

explanation.surface: A deep rumble slowly building over time.
explanation.definitionFit: A deep rumbling noise such as an angry dog makes is a low sound.

clue.text: Where Africans continue to gossip

parts.note: to gab is to chatter or gossip
on means continuing, as in carry on

explanation.surface: A place where people from Africa keep chatting.
explanation.walkthrough: To 'gab on' is to keep gossiping, so the chatter comes before the carrying on. GABON is a country in west-central Africa.
explanation.definitionFit: Gabon is a country on Africa's west coast, home to Africans.

clue.text: Oil-producer has nothing pressing

parts.note: nothing is zero, shaped like the letter O
a live issue is a pressing one

explanation.surface: An oil supplier has nothing to squeeze.
explanation.walkthrough: 'pressing' suggests squeezing oil from fruit, but here means urgent.
explanation.definitionFit: Its fruit is pressed to yield oil, so this tree is an oil-producer.

clue.text: High unknown quantity below roof-space

indicators.note: below places the first piece after the second in a down answer

parts.note: the space under a roof is the loft
in algebra x, y and z stand for unknowns

explanation.surface: Something unknown lies high up beneath the attic.
explanation.definitionFit: Lofty means tall or elevated.

clue.text: Clumsily sat on a piece of piano-music

indicators.note: clumsily suggests the words sat on a are jumbled awkwardly

explanation.surface: Someone sat awkwardly on a sheet of piano music.
explanation.definitionFit: A classical composition in several movements, often for piano, is a sonata.

clue.text: Run rings round chump at Oxford University

parts.note: a chump is a fool or twit

explanation.surface: A fool at Oxford is circling a running track.
explanation.definitionFit: To run rings round someone is to get the better of them by cleverness.

clue.text: Prime cheese set before female

indicators.note: set before places the cheese ahead of the female in the answer

parts.note: brie is a soft French cheese

explanation.surface: Top-quality cheese is served to a woman.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Prime' looks like an adjective meaning excellent but is the verb, to prepare someone with information.
explanation.definitionFit: To prime someone with facts in advance is to instruct them before a task.

clue.text: Cubist roughly depicting small restaurant

indicators.note: depicting means showing, so the answer is shown within the words Cubist roughly

explanation.surface: A Cubist painter roughly sketches a little café.
explanation.definitionFit: A modest informal eatery is a small restaurant.

clue.text: Hide paintings of military display?

explanation.surface: Concealing artworks during a military parade.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Hide' looks like a verb but is skin; a TATTOO is also an evening military show, as at Edinburgh.
explanation.definitionFit: Ink pictures on skin are one sense; a ceremonial drill performance by troops is the other.

clue.text: Vehemently deny England's opener is poor!

indicators.note: vehemently suggests a violent shake-up of the letters
opener means the first letter of the word England's

explanation.surface: Fiercely rejecting the idea that the England opening batsman is no good.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Vehemently' mixes DENY with E, the first letter of England's.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone in want or lacking money is poor.

clue.text: One in three, perhaps? No, two!

indicators.note: in places one inside the shuffled letters
perhaps suggests the word three is one possible arrangement of other letters

parts.note: one is I in Roman numerals

explanation.surface: A quiz guess, one out of three, is corrected to one of two.
explanation.walkthrough: 'perhaps' turns THREE into ETHER, and 'in' puts I (one) inside.
explanation.definitionFit: The word refers to one or the other of a pair, not of three.

clue.text: Canoe revealed by archaeologist?

explanation.surface: A boat unearthed on an excavation.
explanation.definitionFit: A boat hollowed from a log is one sense; something excavated is the other.

clue.text: Women warm up cereal

parts.note: to warm up is to heat

explanation.surface: Women reheat their breakfast cereal.
explanation.definitionFit: A grain grown for flour is a cereal crop.

clue.text: Fierce argument dropping returning aid to the clan

indicators.note: dropping takes those letters out of the longer word

parts.note: a diatribe is a bitter verbal attack

indicators.note: returning means the word aid is read backwards

parts.note: aid is used as written

explanation.surface: A heated row about cutting back aid to a clan.
explanation.walkthrough: 'returning' turns AID into DIA, which 'dropping' removes from DIATRIBE.
explanation.definitionFit: A tribe is a group of related families, much like a clan.

clue.text: Greet tousled bird on the shore

indicators.note: tousled means ruffled, so the letters of greet are messed up

explanation.surface: Welcome a ruffled seabird on the beach.
explanation.definitionFit: A white heron wading on coasts and marshes is a shore bird.

clue.text: Sheer variety here in Surrey

indicators.note: variety suggests a different form of the letters of sheer

explanation.surface: There is sheer diversity to be found in this part of Surrey.
explanation.walkthrough: ESHER is a commuter town in Surrey, a county south-west of London.
explanation.definitionFit: This town lies in Surrey, so it is a place there.

clue.text: Half the doings disguised in this stagecraft

indicators.note: disguised suggests the letters of half the doings are hidden in a new arrangement

explanation.surface: A conjuror conceals half of what he does in his stage act.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Half' looks like a halving instruction but is anagram fodder.
explanation.definitionFit: Manual dexterity in conjuring tricks is a kind of stagecraft.

clue.text: Senior civil servant close a line?

parts.note: close means secretive or private
RY is the abbreviation for railway, a line

explanation.surface: Asking whether a top official should close off a railway line.
explanation.walkthrough: A Permanent Secretary heads a British government department.
explanation.definitionFit: A Permanent Secretary is the top official in a government department.
